paper.citation: Jones, J., Ertefaie, A. and Strawderman, R. L. (2025). Causal mediation analysis: selection with asymptotically valid inference. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology 87(3), 678-700. DOI: 10.1093/jrsssb/qkae109.
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
paper.source_locator: Section 5 'Simulation Studies', arXiv:2110.06127v2 PDF page 15 (the two forms of mu_D0, psi_M and psi_Y, and the three-letter scenario naming; this contribution registers LNN), and Appendix A 'Simulation Results', PDF page 26 (all variances, dimensions and the structural parameters alpha_0, beta_0, gamma_0, and the statement NIE = 2.4). Structural model (1) is on PDF page 4; Proposition 2.1 giving NDE = gamma_0 and NIE = alpha_0 . beta_0 is on PDF page 6.

mechanism.name: Sparse natural indirect effect with ten candidate mediators, scenario LNN (linear propensity, nonlinear mediator confounding, nonlinear outcome confounding)

generation_equations.label: Mediator vector
generation_equations.expression: M = alpha_0 D + psi_M(X) 1_p + eta, eta_j ~ N(0, 1) independently, p = 10, alpha_0 = (1, 2, 2, 0, ..., 0)

generation_equations.label: Outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y = gamma_0 D + beta_0' M + psi_Y(X) + epsilon, epsilon ~ N(0, 1), gamma_0 = 2, beta_0 = (0.8, 0.4, 0.4, 0, ..., 0)

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; X, then D, then the ten-dimensional mediator vector, then Y are generated in temporal order within an individual

assumptions: Consistency and well-defined joint interventions on the treatment and the mediator vector
Treatment exchangeability given X and mediator-outcome exchangeability given (X, D), as encoded by the source's additive model and its Assumptions 2.1 and 2.2
The source's sparsity assumptions: the first three mediators form the good mediator set S*, and no mediator outside S* is related to any variable in S*
Mean-zero errors conditional on the preceding variables: E(eta|X,D) = 0 and E(epsilon|X,D,M) = 0

Treatment positivity: the source states it deliberately chose the small covariate variance 1/4 to minimise the chance of inadvertent positivity violations; expit of a bounded linear or product term stays strictly inside (0,1) for every finite X, but no uniform overlap bound is claimed on unbounded Gaussian support

The source notes that under slightly more general assumptions its estimands also admit an interventional-effect interpretation; the registered definition follows the natural-effect reading the source adopts

properties.notes: Three baseline confounders X1, X2, X3 ~ N(0, 1/4) independently; all three enter psi_M and psi_Y and the first two enter the propensity, so dimension = effective_dimension = 3. The ten candidate mediators are post-treatment and are NOT counted as covariate dimension; exactly three of them carry both a nonzero treatment coefficient and a nonzero outcome coefficient, so the mediator set is sparse with three active out of ten. Not high dimensional: three confounders and ten mediators against source sample sizes 500 to 4000. interactions = false: scenario LNN contains no product term in any structural equation; the nonlinear forms used elsewhere in this family are powers, not interactions. nonlinear = true for the logistic propensity link, the squared term X1^2 in psi_M, the squared term 2(X1-0.5)^2 in psi_Y; the outcome mean is otherwise linear in (D, M, X).

estimand.name: NIE = alpha_0 . beta_0
estimand.definition: Natural indirect effect through the sparse mediator set: NIE = E[Y(1, M(1))] - E[Y(1, M(0))]. Under the source's additive structural model (its equation (1)) and its Proposition 2.1 this equals the inner product alpha_0 . beta_0 of the treatment-to-mediator and mediator-to-outcome coefficient vectors. The companion natural direct effect equals gamma_0. This is NOT a total effect and NOT a single-mediator indirect effect; ten candidate mediators are generated and only the first three are true mediators.

truth.expression: Natural indirect effect through the sparse mediator set: NIE = E[Y(1, M(1))] - E[Y(1, M(0))]. Under the source's additive structural model (its equation (1)) and its Proposition 2.1 this equals the inner product alpha_0 . beta_0 of the treatment-to-mediator and mediator-to-outcome coefficient vectors. The companion natural direct effect equals gamma_0. This is NOT a total effect and NOT a single-mediator indirect effect; ten candidate mediators are generated and only the first three are true mediators.
truth.derivation: Closed form, and printed by the source. The mediator equation is M = alpha_0 D + psi_M(X) 1 + eta and the outcome equation is Y = gamma_0 D + beta_0' M + psi_Y(X) + epsilon with mean-zero errors, so NIE = beta_0' (E[M(1)] - E[M(0)]) = beta_0' alpha_0 = 1*0.8 + 2*0.4 + 2*0.4 = 2.4 exactly, in this and every other confounding-function scenario of the family. The source states NIE = 2.4 in its Appendix A.

adaptations: Version used: arXiv:2110.06127v2 preprint; the published journal version was not accessible to the collector, so section and page locators refer to the preprint PDF and journal pages 678-700 were not cross-checked.

Only the source's 'Large' parameter setting is registered. The source's 'Small' setting makes alpha_0 and beta_0 depend on the sample size n (contributions of order n^{-1/2}), which is a drifting local parameter sequence rather than a fixed data-generating mechanism, so it is deliberately not registered.

SCENARIO SLICING: the source gives a linear and a nonlinear form for each of mu_D0, psi_M and psi_Y and names scenarios by the three-letter triple in that order, mentioning LNN explicitly as an example, which makes eight combinations possible. A change of functional form is a change of mechanism rather than a change of a parameter, so a triple is a contribution rather than a scenario inside one. THREE of the eight are registered, deliberately and not exhaustively, as a reference triple plus its two one-factor neighbours: LNN, the only triple the source names; NNN, which differs from LNN in mu_D0 alone and is the only registered pack carrying the source's X1 * X2 product term; and LNL, which differs from LNN in psi_Y alone. Each registered pair therefore isolates a single nuisance function. The remaining five triples are NOT submitted: they would add relabellings of the same family and inflate the mechanism count without adding a distinct data law. All three share the mechanism_family_id 'jones-2024-robinson-additive-sparse-mediator-selection', so a reviewer who prefers to count the family as a single DGP can collapse them. The source does not state which of the eight combinations it actually ran, and no functional form beyond the two it prints is invented here. This one is LNN.

The source sets p = 10 candidate mediators in the main text and reports a p = 60 setting in its Appendix B. Only p = 10 is registered: the p = 60 variant shares the functional forms of the p = 10 LNN pack and differs only in that dimension, so registering it as a separate mechanism would be a parameter sweep rather than a new data law. It is kept out of the submission for that reason.

The source also uses cross-fitting with K = 10 folds, a perturbation bootstrap with exponential weights, and five competing estimators. All of that is estimation machinery applied to the same data; none of it is reproduced and none is registered as a separate mechanism.
Sampling is re-implemented with NumPy Generator(PCG64); no attempt is made to match the source software draw-for-draw.
